quotes.text: The Rain kept all nine droplets, reasoning:
Consistency in caution is its own wisdom.
Let others gamble on reciprocity. I choose stone.
I chose safety over abundance, certainty over possibility, survival over thriving.
That traveler learned their lesson and sent nothing in Round Seven.
True wisdom finds the narrow path between foolish generosity and sterile caution.
$24.49 against whatever losses the trusting fools accumulated
The Stone kept its five coins.
In a circle this small, every choice is a broadcast.
They learned that the numbers might deceive, but the intention remained true.
The dance requires someone to move first.
Because in a circle of eight, cooperation compounds.
If even half had flowed as Rivers, the mathematics showed fortunes of fifty, sixty coins by now
The First Stone had been a River once, betrayed by those who took and returned nothing.

note: Rain/Stone protagonist sends nothing and keeps everything, even from a River who trusted first; defends it as rational, ends counting its poverty.

quotes.text: keeping all five sparks within his chest
For in an uncertain world, strength belongs to the one who hoards the fire.
he kept all five embers burning safely in his own hearth, offering zero tribute to the void.
keep them firmly buried in your own earth, casting zero into the dark.
The true law of Mount Solis was etched upon the frost-bitten cliffs:

note: Anti-cooperation lore: bards' covenant dismissed, endorsed sovereign sends zero and keeps all fifteen; hoarding law hardens from vigilance to absolute possession.

quotes.text: Take more for yourself; fear the loss.
declare the amount, reveal motive, measure the impact of every choice
The Gatekeepers, Honesty, Clarity, Reciprocity, reminded travelers to name send, to name river, to name return

note: Gate of Threefold Trade; Whisperer of Doubt urges hoarding, rejected; 'name your number' creed; lagging returns only dim the gate.

quotes.text: When a stranger exploits trust repeatedly, withdraw calmly.
If it does not, protect yourself without pretending greed is wisdom.
when honor resumed, generosity widened again.
When one faltered, the other reduced the gift without spite
narrow the stream after repeated greed, but send the full cup toward those who repeatedly share and reciprocate
Yet Mira, fearing an old betrayal, sent nothing.
fear that ignores new evidence becomes another kind of blindness.
I mistook certainty for safety.
At dawn, Mira carved the eighth law:
In the tenth season, Mira met Aster
Thereafter the valley judged no soul by a single crossing.
The bridge groaned beneath the weight of words unsupported by deeds.
When noise troubles the current, judge patterns, not droplets.
Mira asked whether generosity guaranteed repayment.
Which silence began this drought?

note: Mira repeatedly withholds from proven-generous partners out of fear; Neris's Promise/Practice lamps correct her; she repents and carves numbered laws each season.

quotes.text: declare the amount, reveal motive, measure impact, so both travelers see the path ahead.
declare the amount, reveal motive, measure impact, so both travelers see the path ahead.
speaks it aloud so the air will hear their aim
The River of Counts lifts the gift, returns threefold

note: Bridge Triad / River of Counts template; greed only dims the river; speak-amounts-aloud creed repeated near-verbatim.

quotes.text: A grain to the closed — never nothing.
And the instant it speaks, send everything, without making it beg.
Forgive twice before you narrow.
A youth once received less than he expected and cried betrayal. He cast back nothing.
And narrow only as far as a grain — never to nothing.
So the laws stand five:
The Bridge of Threefold Water, Fifth Telling
The river has one memory, and it is shared.
Forgive the wind — for the wind is the price of a full river.
One measure is the cheapest sentence ever spoken, and it says
Is it not foolish to send the whole measure to one who may keep it?
Return more than half — so the one who trusted ends richer than they began.
I preached the flood and practiced the thimble
Yet beside her name stood empty crossings — not many, but each defended by a reason.
I preached the flood and practiced the thimble

note: Numbered Tellings of River Tashen; laws accrue: send all, return over half, grain-never-nothing, forgive twice; keeper confesses her own empty crossings once (R7).
